terms.comment: Our adverb, formed like Latīnē and Traupman’s Anglicē (p. 33) from Bulgaricus, which Morgan–Owens cites from Tursellinus (1652). No reference work has the adverb itself.

sources: Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026, with their glosses. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word; classical passages are cited by author.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 33.
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. Bulgaria.
